clue.text: Left in a site away from studio, wants budget

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for left is placed inside the following phrase

parts.note: filming on location means shooting at a real site rather than in a studio

explanation.surface: A film crew shooting at a remote site complains that it wants more money.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget is the sum of money set aside for a purpose, which is exactly an allotted share.

clue.text: A street apart

parts.note: way is a common word for a street, as in Fosse Way

explanation.definitionFit: Being apart from home means being absent from it, the adverbial sense of not present.

clue.text: Waterloo Station's Austrian architect

indicators.note: the possessive 's is read as has, so the station's name holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: The architect behind a famous London railway terminus is named as an Austrian.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the end of Waterloo and the start of Station. Adolf Loos was a pioneering Viennese modernist architect; London's Waterloo is a major railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolf Loos was the Austrian architect famous for the essay Ornament and Crime.

clue.text: Trust able seaman? A loan may depend on it

definitions.text: A loan may depend on it

parts.note: credit means trust, as in giving credit to a story
an able seaman is a rating, a non-commissioned sailor in the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Can a sailor be relied upon? A bank lending him money will want to know.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenders check a borrower's creditworthiness score before deciding whether to advance money.

clue.text: One is bound by discretion, that's understood

indicators.note: something bound by another is enclosed by it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: tact is discretion in dealing with others
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sworn to discretion makes a quiet understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is understood or implied without being spoken aloud.

clue.text: Title of new wine shop is about right

indicators.note: something about another surrounds it, so the scrambled letters go round the letter for right
new suggests the letters are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: The deeds to a recently opened wine shop are said to be in order.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, title is the right of possession of property, synonymous with legal possession.

clue.text: Hand over after opening of Stock Exchange

indicators.note: after tells us the turned word comes after the opening letter
the opening of a word is its first letter
over means turned round, so the word for hand is read backwards

parts.note: paw is a slang word for a hand

explanation.surface: A trader passes something across once the Stock Exchange opens for business.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange one thing for another is to trade or switch them.

clue.text: Trip over snakes in freak weather conditions

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first word sits above the second

parts.note: a whirl is a short outing or excursion, a quick trip
to snake is to wind, twist and turn

explanation.surface: Someone trips over snakes in the grass during a freak storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Tornadoes and similar violent rotating storms are unusual extreme weather events.

clue.text: Imperious member (Conservative) giving wayward peer support

indicators.note: in a down clue, support means the following pieces sit beneath the first
wayward suggests the letters stray into a new order

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
Tory is the everyday name for a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A haughty Conservative MP backs a peer who has gone off the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: Peremptory means insisting on immediate obedience, domineering and high-handed.

clue.text: Youngster gets rise in benefit? Just the opposite

indicators.note: in signals one piece is placed inside another
this reverses the stated arrangement, so the rise goes round the benefit rather than in it

parts.note: an ascent is a rise or climb
the dole is British slang for state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A young person receives an increase in welfare payments, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says the rise goes into the benefit; 'Just the opposite' swaps the roles, so the benefit goes into the rise instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a teenager, a young person between child and adult.

clue.text: Before end of encounter, draw level

indicators.note: before tells us the word for draw comes ahead of the final letter

parts.note: a tie is a drawn match

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Near the close of a match the teams draw level.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a level or row, as in seating arranged in tiers.

clue.text: Wandering afar, she loves getting drunk

indicators.note: wandering suggests the letters roam into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Roaming far from home, she enjoys getting tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: This old nautical idiom describes someone well on the way to intoxication.

clue.text: Fruit, choice by London station

indicators.note: by means next to, so the word for choice sits beside the station

parts.note: Victoria is a major London railway terminus
plum as an adjective means choice or excellent, as in a plum job

explanation.surface: Fruit picked out at a stall beside a London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known English variety of the stone fruit, red and sweet.

clue.text: Scoring, then withdrawing from field

definitions.meaning: scoring a surface means marking it with lines or grooves
to scratch a horse or competitor is to withdraw it from the field of entrants

explanation.definitionFit: Scratching means both marking a surface and pulling an entrant out of a race.

clue.text: Draw attention to expert holding small coin and cross up

indicators.note: something holding other pieces encloses them

parts.note: an ace is an expert
a cent is a small coin

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tau cross is a T-shaped cross, named after the Greek letter

explanation.surface: An expert grabs a coin and crosses upwards to make a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To accentuate something is to emphasise it, making it stand out.

clue.text: See pest rock violently in vehicle

indicators.note: in tells us the jumbled letters go inside the vehicle

parts.note: a coach is a vehicle

indicators.note: violently suggests the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone watches a bus rock violently and a bug appears.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect is a notorious household pest infesting kitchens.

clue.text: Suddenly everyone's in agreement, including head of committee

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: including means taking a piece inside

parts.note: at one means in agreement

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Without warning, a committee's members all agree, the chair included.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means abruptly, without warning, or simultaneously.

clue.text: Pass quickly across north Welsh town

indicators.note: across means lying over, so the word for pass quickly goes round the letter for north

parts.note: to flit is to move or pass quickly

explanation.surface: Someone darts quickly across north Wales to a small town.
explanation.definitionFit: Flint is a town in north-east Wales, on the Dee estuary.

clue.text: Prevent a check pinning rook

indicators.note: pinning means holding a piece pressed inside

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: In chess, a check that pins the rook could prevent disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert something is to ward it off or prevent it happening.

clue.text: I see what you're saying

parts.note: normally a phrase of understanding, here literally someone who sees spoken words on lips

explanation.definitionFit: A deaf person who reads lips literally sees the words being spoken.

clue.text: Cunning stunt hurt cad in competitive environment

indicators.note: cunning suggests the letters are craftily rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever stunt hurts a cad in a ruthless setting.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom from swordplay describes fierce, lively competition or debate.

clue.text: Religious Education sequence is a repeat

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for Religious Education, a school subject
a run is a sequence, as in a run of wins

explanation.surface: A school's Religious Education programme is shown again on television.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a repeated broadcast of a programme.

clue.text: I spot game

definitions.meaning: spot means see, so this is a literal statement of seeing
the children's guessing game where one player names a letter of an object seen

explanation.definitionFit: The game takes its name from its opening words, said when one spies something.

clue.text: Fist fight in factory

definitions.meaning: an old slang word for a boxing match or fist fight
a ... is a factory, as in a cotton ...

explanation.definitionFit: Mill means both a fist fight in old slang and a factory building.

clue.text: Boy against being embraced by another

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held inside it

parts.note: Ian is another boy's name, the clue having already said boy
V is the abbreviation for versus, against

explanation.surface: One boy is hugged by another.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is a boy's name, the Russian form of John.

clue.text: Like a pantomime dame veteran, sit out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A veteran actor playing a pantomime dame decides to sit this one out.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime dame is a comic female role in British Christmas theatre, traditionally played by a man.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase describes a performer dressed as the opposite sex, as a man in a panto dame role.

clue.text: Information wanted about lake in valley

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for information goes round the letter for lake

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone wants information about a lake in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Girl presented to prince, say, in plant

parts.note: Penny is a girl's name
a prince is an example of a royal

explanation.surface: A girl is presented at court to a prince in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennyroyal is a mint plant, once used in herbal remedies.
